title: OLS and generalized linear models
dek: OLS is MLE for Gaussian errors with identity link. GLMs keep a linear predictor and change the mean–variance marriage.
story: Ordinary least squares models E[Y] = Xβ and estimates β by minimizing ‖Y − Xβ‖². If ε ~ N(0, σ² I), that minimizer is the MLE, θ̂ = (XᵀX)⁻¹ XᵀY when X has full rank, and the residual sum of squares over σ² is a χ² story.

A GLM keeps a linear predictor η = Xβ but lets the mean μ = E[Y] live in a different relationship to η: g(μ) = η for a link g, and lets Var(Y) follow a variance function V(μ) from an exponential family (Gaussian, Bernoulli/binomial, Poisson, gamma, …).

Logistic regression is a Bernoulli GLM with logit link. Poisson regression is a count GLM, often with log link and offset log(exposure). Once you can write those two, most “machine learning classifiers” in a TB paper are GLMs in a hoodie.
deepTitle: Exponential family, IRLS, and what OLS assumptions were actually doing
deep: Exponential family density: f(y | θ, φ) = exp{(yθ − b(θ))/a(φ) + c(y, φ)}. Then μ = b′(θ), Var(Y) = b″(θ) a(φ). The canonical link sets η = θ, which is why logit is canonical for Bernoulli and log is canonical for Poisson.

Fisher scoring / IRLS: iterate a weighted least-squares problem with working response z = η + (y − μ) g′(μ) and weights 1 / (V(μ) g′(μ)²). OLS is the first and last iteration of that procedure in the Gaussian identity case.

Misspecification of V(μ) still leaves consistent β̂ for the mean parameters under a correct mean model (quasi-likelihood), with sandwich SEs. Overdispersed TB cluster counts are the textbook case for quasi-Poisson or a negative binomial, or for a hierarchical Poisson.
The LRT in GLMs is a difference in deviance. Wald uses β̂ / se(β̂). Do not mix a robust SE with a model-based LRT and call them the same test.

Geometry of OLS is orthogonal projection; Gauss–Markov is BLUE inside a small class; diagnostics are how you see a hostage row; omitted variables change the target functional. Those specialised plates sit under this GLM umbrella. IRLS is the algorithm that makes a logit feel like weighted OLS.

formulas.label: OLS / Gaussian MLE
formulas.expression: Y = Xβ + ε,   β̂ = (XᵀX)⁻¹ Xᵀ Y
formulas.note: Identity link, constant variance. Unique if X has full column rank.

formulas.label: GLM
formulas.note: Mean through a link; variance tied to the mean by the family.

visual.caption: Plate notation for a GLM: covariates X are observed, β is a parameter, the linear predictor η is deterministic, and Y is observed with a mean tied to η by the link. The family (Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson) lives in the arrow from η to Y — that is the variance function.

example.title: Logit of smear-positive disease
example.setup: n = 400 TB cases. Y = 1 if smear-positive. Covariates: cavity (0/1), days of cough, HIV. Fit logit π = β₀ + β_cav + β_days + β_hiv. Nested comparison: drop cavity.

steps.title: Mean model
steps.body: π = logit⁻¹(Xβ). Variance is π(1−π) if the Bernoulli model is true; there is no extra σ² to estimate in the strict binomial family (φ = 1).

steps.title: What β_cav is
steps.body: On the log-odds scale: the adjusted log odds ratio for cavitation. Exponentiate only if you want an odds ratio, and do not call it a risk ratio unless π is small.

steps.title: Nested test
steps.body: The LRT for cavity is 2(ℓ_full − ℓ_reduced) vs χ²_1. A Wald p-value on β_cav / se uses a different finite-sample object. With sparse HIV×cavity cells, they can disagree; look at the 2×2 counts.

example.takeaway: Name the link, the variance, and the scale of the coefficient before quoting exp(β).

check.prompt: OLS is a GLM in which:
choices: The link is logit and V(μ) = μ
The link is identity and V(μ) is constant (Gaussian)
check.answer: The link is identity and V(μ) is constant (Gaussian)
check.why: That is the Gaussian identity GLM. Logit+Bernoulli is logistic regression; log+μ variance is Poisson.

whyWrong.The link is logit and V(μ) = μ: A confused mix of logistic and Poisson.

check.prompt: In a Bernoulli GLM, if π̂ = 0.2, what is the model-based Var(Yᵢ)?

whyWrong.0.2: That is the mean, not the Bernoulli variance.

check.prompt: On the GLM plate, ηᵢ is drawn as a diamond (deterministic). What does that mark?
check.figureHint: β is a parameter circle, xᵢ and yᵢ are observed, ηᵢ sits between them.
choices: That ηᵢ is an extra unknown parameter with its own prior
That ηᵢ = xᵢᵀβ is a function of parameters and covariates, not a new source of randomness
That ηᵢ is the only observed node
That OLS forbids a linear predictor
check.answer: That ηᵢ = xᵢᵀβ is a function of parameters and covariates, not a new source of randomness
check.why: Plate notation: filled/observed, empty/parameter, diamond/deterministic. The randomness is in y | η, through the family.

whyWrong.That ηᵢ is an extra unknown parameter wi: That would be another empty circle, perhaps a random effect — the hierarchical plate.
whyWrong.That ηᵢ is the only observed node: x and y are the observed nodes.
whyWrong.That OLS forbids a linear predictor: OLS is the identity-link Gaussian case of this plate.
